name: Monoglass insulation
title: Monoglass insulation: legacy photos | Spray Insulations
desc: See the recovered Monoglass overhead photograph, its source, and the records to gather before planning insulation or repairs.
alt: White-grey overhead fibre insulation above exposed pipework in a commercial interior.
caption: The photograph associated with Monoglass in the original WeSprayIt service section shows overhead fibre insulation above pipework. The earlier white annotation was removed with AI-assisted cleanup; the source original is retained.
intro: The recovered Monoglass photograph is back alongside its material page. Use the overhead view to discuss access, service penetrations and existing conditions; use product records and an assessment to establish what is installed.
sections: The legacy image and its context

The original WeSprayIt service page paired this photograph with its Monoglass section. That association is preserved here. Pipes and suspended services are visible below the coated overhead surface, so photographs for a new enquiry should show both the finish and the obstructions beneath it.

Gather the original specification, product records, drawings and any repair history. Describe the area, access height, occupied use and visible damage. Identify who will review the proposed scope before finishes or services make the work difficult to reach.

A matching colour or texture does not establish the installed material or a compatible repair. Ask the assessor to confirm the existing system and document the proposed preparation, replacement area and inspection arrangements.
faqs: Where did the Monoglass photo come from?
It was recovered from the WeSprayIt archive, where it appeared with the Monoglass service section.
Was the photograph edited?
A white annotation was removed with AI-assisted cleanup. The original file remains available below.
Does the photo identify the installer?
The available record does not establish the legal installer, location or installation date.
Can the photo establish a fire rating or insulation value?
No. Those depend on the identified product, installed assembly and supporting records.
What should I send with an enquiry?
Send your own overall and close-up photographs, location, access details, the reason for the work and any existing specification.

name: HiBar fireproofing
title: HiBar fireproofing: images and planning | Spray Insulations
desc: View the HiBAR manufacturer image and legacy service context, with a checklist for identifying the assembly and planning an assessment.
alt: Textured spray-applied material across roof decking and open steel framing in SOPREMA’s HiBAR image.
caption: SOPREMA identifies this image in its HiBAR product gallery. It shows the overhead finish across decking and open steel framing; it is manufacturer imagery, not a claimed Spray Insulations customer project.
intro: HiBar had a dedicated section in the earlier WeSprayIt service content. This page restores that subject to Spray with an identified HiBAR manufacturer image and practical questions for a project assessment.
sections: HiBar is a separate material topic

SOPREMA describes HiBAR as a spray-applied blend of mineral fibres and binders. Its manufacturer page supplies the current product and technical documents. Foam photographs do not illustrate this material and are not used as substitutes here.

For an existing building, collect drawings, the named product, any assembly reference and previous inspection or repair records. Show the structural members, decking, services and access constraints in your own photographs.

Ask who will confirm the applicable system, preparation and inspection requirements. A written scope should identify the work areas, access arrangements, protection of surrounding surfaces and the records to be supplied at handover. A photo cannot establish a fire-resistance rating.
faqs: Is this HiBar image from a Spray Insulations job?
No. It is credited manufacturer imagery from SOPREMA’s HiBAR product gallery.
Why is HiBar separate from spray foam?
The material and assembly must be identified separately; a foam project photograph is not a HiBar reference.
Where are the current product documents?
Use the linked SOPREMA HiBAR page for its technical and safety documents.
Can I determine the required thickness from this photo?
No. Ask the responsible professional to identify the actual assembly and applicable requirements.
What should a HiBar enquiry include?
Include the building use, work area, drawings or specification, access constraints and photographs of the actual condition.

name: Commercial work archive
title: Commercial overhead work archive | Spray Insulations
desc: Recovered commercial access photography with source credits and practical questions for coating and insulation project planning.
alt: Two scissor lifts inside a large commercial interior beneath overhead work areas.
caption: Recovered commercial job-site photography shows two scissor lifts and overhead access. The available archive does not identify the coating product, contractor or project location.
intro: This recovered commercial-work photograph belongs with the wider coatings and insulation archive. It records the work setting and access equipment; it does not identify a material or prove the finished installation.
sections: Large interiors can combine overhead work, floor access, equipment movement and other trades. This photograph helps explain why an enquiry should show the whole working area as well as the surface being assessed.

Separate the coating or insulation requirement from access, preparation, protection and the return of the area to use. Supply the building use, existing records and photographs of the surfaces. Ask for the proposed system to be named in the quotation.

Keep dated before-and-after photographs with their location and scope notes. Store the specification, agreed changes and handover documents together. An archive photograph is useful context, but is not evidence of a new project’s performance.
faqs: Where is the commercial photograph from?

Does it show a named coating system?

Does this page identify a contractor for the work?

Why show access equipment on an insulation site?
Access and coordination affect the scope of overhead insulation and coatings work.
Where can I read more about coatings planning?
